chunks.heading: Three rules to remember right away
chunks.text: Cells are counted from one. The top-left pixel is (1, 1), not (0, 0). Edges are part of the shape. A rectangle from 1 to 10 is 10 pixels, not 9. Drew it - show it. Drawing only changes memory. To make the picture appear on screen, call canvas:Update() or canvas:EndFrame().

chunks.heading: Documentation site
chunks.text: This documentation also has a terminal-style site in the site folder. You can type commands there, like in Telegram or Discord: /help, /canvas, /fn DrawLine.

chunks.heading: What is Bloom
chunks.text: Bloom is a Roblox library that draws pictures pixel by pixel. A pixel is one tiny colored dot on the screen.

chunks.heading: Imagine a squared notebook
chunks.text: Take a squared notebook and colored pencils. If you color the right squares, you get a picture: a house, the sun, a cat. Bloom works the same way: The canvas (canvas) is the notebook. A pixel is one square. A color is a pencil. Drawing functions (DrawLine, DrawRectangle and others) are helpers. They color many squares at once: a whole line or a whole rectangle. 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 ← column number (x) 1 . . . . . . . . 2 . ■ ■ ■ ■ ■ . . ← DrawRectangle(2, 2, 6, 4, ...) 3 . ■ ■ ■ ■ ■ . . 4 . ■ ■ ■ ■ ■ . . 5 . . . . . . . . ↑ row number (y)

chunks.heading: Where the picture lives
chunks.text: Bloom keeps two "copies" of the picture. The draft in memory. This is a buffer, a long strip of numbers. Every square takes 4 numbers in it: red, green, blue and transparency. All drawing functions draw only here. It is very fast, but nothing is visible on screen yet. The picture on screen. This is an EditableImage, a special Roblox image that can be changed from code. A regular ImageLabel shows it. When you call canvas:Update(), Bloom moves the draft to the screen. It is like a drawing you first sketch in pencil on scrap paper and then carefully copy into your album. DrawLine, DrawRectangle, ... Update() / EndFrame() ───────────────────────────► draft (buffer) ─────────────► screen (EditableImage)

chunks.heading: Why the canvas is cut into pieces
chunks.text: Roblox has a rule: one EditableImage cannot be bigger than 1024 × 1024 pixels. If you need a bigger canvas, for example 2000 × 1500, Bloom cuts it into tiles, like a floor made of tiles. Every tile is a separate EditableImage with its own ImageLabel. Together they look like one big picture. canvas 2000 × 1500 with tile_size = 1024 ┌──────────┬───────┐ │ tile 0 │ til.1 │ 1024 + 976 = 2000 ├──────────┼───────┤ │ tile 2 │ til.3 │ 1024 + 476 = 1500 └──────────┴───────┘ When you draw, Bloom remembers which tiles you touched. Such tiles are called "dirty". On update, Bloom sends only the dirty tiles to the screen and leaves the rest alone. That is faster.

chunks.heading: What Bloom can do
chunks.text: Ability Chapter Dots, lines, soft thick lines, rectangles, triangles Drawing Copying ready pictures, stretching, tinting, transparency Textures Filters: invert, black and white, brightness, your own filters Shaders Text from .ttf fonts or from your own letter pictures Fonts and text A task queue with priorities so there is no lag Scheduler Your own code at different moments of a frame Pipeline Speed counters Stats

chunks.heading: What Bloom cannot do
chunks.text: Bloom draws on the processor (CPU), not on the graphics card. So a big canvas where every pixel changes every frame will be slow. Bloom is good for interfaces, minimaps, pixel art, charts and effects on small areas. It is not a 3D engine. Bloom draws only flat 2D pictures. Bloom shaders are regular Luau functions. They run on the processor, not on the graphics card. Bloom must not be called from several threads at once for the same canvas.

chunks.heading: Where to put the code
chunks.text: Bloom is needed where the player sees the picture, that is in a LocalScript on the client. An EditableImage is not sent from the server to players. If you create it on the server, the player will not see it. StarterPlayer └── StarterPlayerScripts └── MyDrawing (LocalScript) ← call Bloom here ReplicatedStorage └── Bloom (ModuleScript) ← the library lives here Next: Setup and check →

chunks.heading: Setup and check
chunks.text: Before drawing you need to do three things: Put the library into the game. Allow the game to use EditableImage. Check that everything works.

chunks.heading: Step 1. Put the library into the game
chunks.text: Bloom is the src folder. In Roblox it must become one ModuleScript named Bloom, with other modules inside it. ReplicatedStorage └── Bloom (ModuleScript, code from src/init.luau) ├── async (ModuleScript, src/async.luau) ├── color4 (ModuleScript, src/color4.luau) ├── font (ModuleScript, src/font.luau) ├── pipeline (ModuleScript, src/pipeline.luau) ├── shader (ModuleScript, src/shader.luau) ├── support (ModuleScript, src/support.luau) ├── texture (ModuleScript, src/texture.luau) ├── types (ModuleScript, src/types.luau) └── elements (ModuleScript, src/elements/init.luau) ├── line (ModuleScript, src/elements/line.luau) ├── pixel (ModuleScript, src/elements/pixel.luau) ├── rect (ModuleScript, src/elements/rect.luau) └── triangle (ModuleScript, src/elements/triangle.luau)

chunks.heading: Option A: with Rojo (easy)
chunks.text: Rojo turns the src folder into these modules for you. In your Rojo project file, set "$path": "src" for the Bloom object inside ReplicatedStorage.

chunks.heading: Option B: by hand
chunks.text: Create a ModuleScript named Bloom in ReplicatedStorage and paste the code from src/init.luau. Inside Bloom, create the modules from the list above and paste each file's code into it. Inside elements, create the modules line, pixel, rect and triangle. Names must match exactly, in lowercase. Bloom finds modules by name: require("@self/types") means "my child module named types". If you name the module Types with a capital letter, you get a "module not found" error.

chunks.heading: Step 2. Allow EditableImage
chunks.text: By default Roblox forbids published games from changing images from code. This protects players. You only need to turn the permission on once.

chunks.heading: In Roblox Studio
chunks.text: Open File → Experience Settings. Choose Security on the left. Turn on Allow Mesh / Image APIs. Press Save.

chunks.heading: For a published game
chunks.text: Open the Creator Dashboard. Choose your game → Configure → Settings. Turn on Enable Mesh / Image APIs. This toggle is only available to accounts that are 13+ and have passed ID verification. If the toggle is grey, the account is not verified yet.

chunks.heading: Step 3. Check that everything works
chunks.text: Bloom has a built-in check. It creates a tiny 1 × 1 image, tries to write a pixel into it and read it back, and then deletes it right away. If something fails, Bloom tells you what exactly. Bloom.Create runs this check by itself. If EditableImage is disabled, you will see a clear error that tells you which toggle to turn on. You can also run the check in advance, for example to show the player a message instead of an error.

chunks.heading: Bloom.CheckSupport()
chunks.text: What it does: checks whether this game can use EditableImage right now. No canvas is created. Arguments: none. Returns: a report table (it is frozen, you cannot change it): Field Type Meaning supported boolean true - everything works, you can draw status string "supported", "disabled" or "out_of_memory" message string An explanation of what happened and what to do details string? The exact Roblox error text, if there was one Example: local Bloom = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.Bloom) local report = Bloom.CheckSupport() if report.supported then print("Ready to draw!") elseif report.status == "disabled" then warn("Turn on Allow Mesh / Image APIs in the game settings") warn(report.details) elseif report.status == "out_of_memory" then warn("This device is out of image memory") end All outcomes: ✅ status = "supported" - the image was created, written and read. This answer is remembered: next calls return it right away without a new check. 🚫 status = "disabled" - Roblox raised an error while creating, writing or reading the image. Almost always this means the Allow Mesh / Image APIs toggle is off. details holds the exact Roblox error text. This answer is not remembered: turn the toggle on and the next check will pass. 🧠 status = "out_of_memory" - Roblox returned nil instead of an image. This happens when the device (usually a weak phone) is out of image memory. Delete unneeded EditableImage objects and check again. This answer is not remembered either. 🧪 The test image is always deleted, so the check does not waste memory.

chunks.heading: Bloom.IsSupported()
chunks.text: What it does: the same as CheckSupport, but answers just "yes" or "no". Returns: boolean - true if EditableImage works. if not Bloom.IsSupported() then return end All outcomes: ✅ true - you can draw. 🚫 false - you cannot. Bloom.CheckSupport().status shows why.

chunks.heading: Bloom.Support.Assert()
chunks.text: What it does: runs the check and, if something is wrong, stops the script with an error that has a clear text. Bloom.Create calls it by itself. All outcomes: ✅ Everything works - the function does nothing and the script continues. 🚫 EditableImage is disabled - an error like Bloom: EditableImage is not available in this experience. In Studio open File > Experience Settings > Security and enable 'Allow Mesh / Image APIs'. ... (Roblox error text). 🧠 Not enough memory - the error Bloom: EditableImage memory budget is exhausted on this device; ....

chunks.heading: All together: a safe start
chunks.text: local Players = game:GetService("Players") local Bloom = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.Bloom) local report = Bloom.CheckSupport() if not report.supported then warn("[My game] Drawing is unavailable: " .. report.status) return end local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui") screenGui.Parent = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui") local template = Instance.new("ImageLabel") template.BackgroundTransparency = 1 local canvas = Bloom.Create(Vector2.new(256, 256), screenGui, template) Next: First picture →

chunks.heading: Step 1. Create a LocalScript
chunks.text: In StarterPlayer → StarterPlayerScripts create a LocalScript and name it FirstPicture. The Bloom library must be in ReplicatedStorage (see Setup).

chunks.heading: Step 2. Load the library and colors
chunks.text: local Players = game:GetService("Players") local Bloom = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.Bloom) local Color4 = Bloom.GetColor4() Color4 is a box of pencils. Color4.New32Bit(red, green, blue) makes a color. Every number goes from 0 (none at all) to 255 (as much as possible). local SKY = Color4.New32Bit(135, 206, 235) local GRASS = Color4.New32Bit(60, 170, 70) local WALL = Color4.New32Bit(230, 180, 120) local ROOF = Color4.New32Bit(190, 60, 50) local WINDOW = Color4.New32Bit(255, 255, 200) local DOOR = Color4.New32Bit(110, 70, 40) local SUN = Color4.New32Bit(255, 220, 0)

chunks.heading: Step 3. Make a place where the picture is visible
chunks.text: local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui") screenGui.Name = "FirstPicture" screenGui.Parent = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui") local frame = Instance.new("Frame") frame.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(256, 192) frame.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(40, 40) frame.Parent = screenGui local template = Instance.new("ImageLabel") template.BackgroundTransparency = 1 frame is the picture frame. The picture appears inside it. template is a sample. Bloom copies it for every tile of the canvas. You do not need to put the sample anywhere.

chunks.heading: Step 4. Create the canvas
chunks.text: local canvas = Bloom.Create(Vector2.new(256, 192), frame, template) Now you have a notebook 256 squares wide and 192 squares tall.

chunks.heading: Step 5. Draw!
chunks.text: canvas:BeginFrame(SKY) canvas:DrawRectangle(1, 160, 256, 192, GRASS) canvas:DrawRectangle(60, 100, 140, 160, WALL) canvas:DrawTriangle(50, 100, 150, 100, 100, 55, ROOF) canvas:DrawRectangle(72, 112, 90, 128, WINDOW) canvas:DrawRectangle(110, 112, 128, 128, WINDOW) canvas:DrawRectangle(92, 132, 108, 160, DOOR) canvas:DrawRectangle(205, 20, 225, 40, SUN) canvas:DrawLineAA(215, 5, 215, 55, 2, SUN) canvas:DrawLineAA(190, 30, 240, 30, 2, SUN) canvas:EndFrame() What happens here: BeginFrame(SKY) fills the whole sheet with blue sky. DrawRectangle(1, 160, 256, 192, GRASS) - green grass at the bottom, from the left edge to the right edge. Walls, a triangle roof, windows, a door. The sun - a square and two soft lines as rays. EndFrame() shows everything on screen.

chunks.heading: Step 6. Press Play
chunks.text: Press Play in Studio. A house appears in the top-left corner!

chunks.heading: If nothing appeared
chunks.text: What you see Why What to do An Allow Mesh / Image APIs error The EditableImage permission is off Turn it on following the guide No errors, but empty You forgot EndFrame() or Update() Add canvas:EndFrame() at the end Empty and the frame is white You did not pass template Pass an ImageLabel as the third argument An attempt to index nil error The script is a regular Script, not a LocalScript Use a LocalScript Only a part is visible The frame is smaller than the canvas, the rest is clipped Make frame.Size equal to the canvas size

chunks.heading: Full code
chunks.text: local Players = game:GetService("Players") local Bloom = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.Bloom) local Color4 = Bloom.GetColor4() local SKY = Color4.New32Bit(135, 206, 235) local GRASS = Color4.New32Bit(60, 170, 70) local WALL = Color4.New32Bit(230, 180, 120) local ROOF = Color4.New32Bit(190, 60, 50) local WINDOW = Color4.New32Bit(255, 255, 200) local DOOR = Color4.New32Bit(110, 70, 40) local SUN = Color4.New32Bit(255, 220, 0) local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui") screenGui.Name = "FirstPicture" screenGui.Parent = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui") local frame = Instance.new("Frame") frame.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(256, 192) frame.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(40, 40) frame.Parent = screenGui local template = Instance.new("ImageLabel") template.BackgroundTransparency = 1 local canvas = Bloom.Create(Vector2.new(256, 192), frame, template) canvas:BeginFrame(SKY) canvas:DrawRectangle(1, 160, 256, 192, GRASS) canvas:DrawRectangle(60, 100, 140, 160, WALL) canvas:DrawTriangle(50, 100, 150, 100, 100, 55, ROOF) canvas:DrawRectangle(72, 112, 90, 128, WINDOW) canvas:DrawRectangle(110, 112, 128, 128, WINDOW) canvas:DrawRectangle(92, 132, 108, 160, DOOR) canvas:DrawRectangle(205, 20, 225, 40, SUN) canvas:DrawLineAA(215, 5, 215, 55, 2, SUN) canvas:DrawLineAA(190, 30, 240, 30, 2, SUN) canvas:EndFrame() script.Destroying:Connect(function() canvas:Destroy() end)

chunks.heading: Animation: drawing every frame
chunks.text: To make a picture move, you redraw it many times per second. local RunService = game:GetService("RunService") local x = 1 RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function() canvas:BeginFrame(SKY) canvas:DrawRectangle(x, 80, x + 20, 100, SUN) canvas:EndFrame() x = if x > 236 then 1 else x + 1 end) Do not create the canvas inside RenderStepped! Create it once and only draw in the loop. Creating a canvas is expensive. Next: Canvas in detail →

chunks.heading: Canvas
chunks.text: The canvas (canvas) is the main Bloom object. It holds the pixel draft, the screen tiles, the settings, the task queue and the pipeline. All drawing goes through it.

chunks.heading: How a frame works
chunks.text: BeginFrame(color?) → draw → EndFrame() │ │ ├─ stage "beginFrame" ├─ stage "endFrame" └─ fill, if a color is given └─ Update() or UpdateAsync()

chunks.heading: Useful canvas fields
chunks.text: You can read them, but do not change them by hand: there are functions for that. Field What it is canvas.res_x Canvas width in pixels canvas.res_y Canvas height in pixels canvas.tile_size Size of one tile canvas.size_x, canvas.size_y How many tiles across and down canvas.tiles Tiles (number → {x, y, w, h, editable, buffer, image}) canvas.async This canvas's task scheduler (chapter 10) canvas.pipeline Stage pipeline (chapter 11)

chunks.heading: Bloom.Create(resolution, parent?, reference?, options?)
chunks.text: What it does: creates a new canvas. If you pass parent and reference, the picture appears on screen. Arguments: Name Type Required? What it is resolution Vector2 yes Canvas size in pixels, for example Vector2.new(320, 240). The fractional part is dropped parent Instance? no Where to put the images: Frame, ScreenGui, SurfaceGui and so on reference ImageLabel? no A sample. Bloom copies it for every tile options Options? no Extra settings (see the table below) options settings: Field Default What it does tile_size 1024 Tile size. The number is rounded down and clamped between 1 and 1024 async_budget 0.002 How many seconds the scheduler may work per step. Never less than 0.0001 scheduler_options {} Scheduler settings (chapter 10) auto_clip true Turn on ClipsDescendants on parent so the picture does not stick out of the frame clear_color 0 The color for Clear() without an argument. 0 is fully transparent Returns: a canvas (Bloom). Example: local canvas = Bloom.Create(Vector2.new(320, 240), frame, template, { tile_size = 512, clear_color = Color4.New32Bit(20, 20, 30), }) All outcomes: ✅ parent and reference are given. A copy of reference is made for every tile. It gets a size in pixels (UDim2.fromOffset), a position, ImageContent and Visible = true, and then it is put into parent. One canvas pixel equals one screen pixel. 🌑 No reference. The canvas draws "invisibly": everything works, but nothing appears on screen. This is handy for preparing pictures in advance or for computing something from pixels. 👻 reference is given, but no parent. The copies are created but not put anywhere, so they are not visible. ✂️ parent is a GuiObject (for example a Frame) and auto_clip is not turned off. Then ClipsDescendants = true is set on parent. A ScreenGui does not have this property, and Bloom leaves it alone. 🧩 The canvas is bigger than tile_size. It is cut into tiles. Tiles in the last column and the last row may be smaller than the others. 🎨 Starting color. A new canvas is fully transparent (all pixels are 0), even if clear_color is set. To fill it with that color, call canvas:Clear(). 🧼 Dirty tiles. Right after creation all tiles are "dirty", so the first Update() sends them all to the screen. 🚫 Size less than 1 (for example Vector2.new(0, 100)) - the error Bloom.Create expects a positive resolution. 🚫 EditableImage is disabled in the game settings - an error with a hint about Allow Mesh / Image APIs (chapter 2). 🧠 Out of memory. The error Bloom: EditableImage memory budget is exhausted (WxH tile). Bloom deletes all tiles it managed to create before the error by itself, so no memory leaks.

chunks.heading: Bloom.FromEditableImage(editable_image, holder)
chunks.text: What it does: turns an existing EditableImage into a canvas. The image's pixels are copied into the draft, so you can draw on top of them. Arguments: Name Type What it is editable_image EditableImage Your image, at most 1024 × 1024 holder ImageLabel The ImageLabel that already shows this image Returns: a canvas. local editable = AssetService:CreateEditableImage({ Size = Vector2.new(128, 128) }) imageLabel.ImageContent = Content.fromObject(editable) local canvas = Bloom.FromEditableImage(editable, imageLabel) canvas:DrawLine(1, 1, 128, 128, Color4.New32Bit(255, 0, 0)) canvas:Update() All outcomes: ✅ The canvas gets one tile - your image. Its current pixels become the draft. 🔒 The image and the ImageLabel stay yours: canvas:Destroy() does not delete them. 🧼 The tile is not dirty right away: your image is already on screen. It updates after the first drawing. 🚫 The image is bigger than 1024 on any side - the error Bloom.FromEditableImage supports images up to 1024x1024. 🚫 The image size is 0 - the error Bloom.FromEditableImage expects a positive resolution. 🚫 You cannot call Resize later - it raises an error (see below). ℹ️ This function does not check the game settings. If you already have an EditableImage, they are turned on.

chunks.heading: canvas:BeginFrame(clear_color?)
chunks.text: What it does: starts a new frame. If you pass a color, the whole canvas is filled with it first. Name Type What it is clear_color number? Fill color. If you do not pass it, the canvas is not cleared All outcomes: ✅ A color is given - Clear(color) runs, then the beginFrame stage runs. ✅ No color - the old picture stays, only the beginFrame stage runs. 💤 The canvas is already destroyed - nothing happens. BeginFrame() without an argument does not fill the canvas even with the color from SetClearColor. If you want clearing with the default color, call canvas:Clear().

chunks.heading: canvas:EndFrame(use_async?)
chunks.text: What it does: finishes the frame and shows it on screen. Name Type What it is use_async boolean? true - send piece by piece with UpdateAsync(). Otherwise everything is sent at once with Update() All outcomes: ✅ The endFrame stage runs, then Update() or UpdateAsync(). 💤 The canvas is destroyed - nothing happens.

chunks.heading: canvas:Update()
chunks.text: What it does: sends all dirty tiles to the screen right now. All outcomes: ✅ Stages run in this order: beforeUpload → uploading every dirty tile → afterUpload. The tiles become clean. ✋ If some tiles were waiting to be sent through UpdateAsync, that waiting is cancelled: Update sends them itself. ⚠️ A tile could not be sent (Roblox raised an error) - the warning [Bloom] Failed to upload tile N: ... appears. The tile stays dirty and tries again next time. Other tiles are sent as usual. 💤 No dirty tiles - the stages still run, but nothing is uploaded. 💤 The canvas is destroyed - nothing happens. 🐢 Roblox updates one EditableImage on screen per frame. If there are 4 dirty tiles, the picture may need 4 frames to catch up. This is a Roblox rule, not a Bloom bug.

chunks.heading: canvas:UpdateAsync(budget?)
chunks.text: What it does: puts the dirty tiles into the scheduler queue. Every tile is a separate task. The work is spread over time, and the game does not freeze. Name Type What it is budget number? How many seconds the scheduler may work per step. Remembered forever (minimum 0.0001) All outcomes: ✅ beforeUpload runs, every dirty tile joins the queue, and the scheduler starts. 📦 After every uploaded tile the tileUploaded stage runs. After the last one - afterUpload. 🔁 A tile is already in the queue - it is not added a second time. The pixels are taken at the moment of sending, so the freshest ones go out. 💤 No dirty tiles - afterUpload runs right away and the scheduler does not start. ✋ Update(), Resize() or Destroy() cancel this queue. ⚠️ The scheduler is shared: together with tiles it also runs your tasks from canvas:Submit. 💤 The canvas is destroyed - nothing happens.

chunks.heading: canvas:Clear(color?)
chunks.text: What it does: fills the whole canvas with one color. Name Type What it is color number? The color. If you do not pass it, the color from SetClearColor (or clear_color from the settings) is used All outcomes: ✅ The whole canvas is painted, all tiles are dirty. 🖼️ The drawing window (SetViewport) does not apply: everything is cleared. ⚡ The color 0 is filled especially fast. 💤 The canvas is destroyed - nothing happens.

chunks.heading: canvas:SetClearColor(color)
chunks.text: What it does: remembers the color that Clear() uses without an argument. canvas:SetClearColor(Color4.New32Bit(0, 0, 0)) canvas:Clear() All outcomes: ✅ the color is remembered. The canvas itself does not change.

chunks.heading: Drawing window (viewport)
chunks.text: A viewport is a stencil frame. Everything drawn outside of it is clipped. ┌────────────── canvas ─────────────┐ │ │ │ ┌── viewport ──┐ │ │ │ you can │ │ │ │ draw here │ │ │ └──────────────┘ │ └───────────────────────────────────┘

chunks.heading: canvas:SetViewport(x, y, width, height)
chunks.text: Name Type What it is x, y number Top-left corner of the window (from 1) width, height number Width and height of the window canvas:SetViewport(10, 10, 100, 50) canvas:DrawRectangle(1, 1, 500, 500, RED) canvas:ResetViewport() All outcomes: ✅ The window is set. Numbers are rounded down. ✂️ The window sticks out of the canvas - it is cut to the canvas edges. 🕳️ Width or height is 0 or less, or the window is fully outside the canvas - the window is empty, and nothing is drawn until you call ResetViewport. ℹ️ These respect the window: DrawPixel, all lines, rectangles, triangles, textures, text and shaders. ℹ️ These ignore the window: Clear, ReadPixel, DrawPixelUnsafe, ReadPixelUnsafe and direct writes into GetBuffer().

chunks.heading: canvas:ResetViewport()
chunks.text: What it does: sets the window back to the whole canvas. All outcomes: ✅ you can draw everywhere again.

chunks.heading: canvas:GetState()
chunks.text: What it does: returns the live state table { clear_color, viewport = { x, y, w, h } }. All outcomes: ✅ the table is not a copy but the original. If you change its fields, the canvas changes too. Better use SetViewport and SetClearColor.

chunks.heading: canvas:GetBuffer()
chunks.text: What it does: gives you the draft itself - the buffer that holds all pixels. How to find a pixel in the buffer: offset = ((y - 1) * canvas.res_x + (x - 1)) * 4. local pixels = canvas:GetBuffer() local offset = ((5 - 1) * canvas.res_x + (3 - 1)) * 4 buffer.writeu32(pixels, offset, Color4.New32Bit(255, 0, 0)) canvas:MarkDirty(3, 5, 3, 5) canvas:Update() All outcomes: ✅ You can read and write directly. This is the fastest way. ⚠️ Bloom does not know that you changed something. Always call MarkDirty, otherwise the changes do not appear on screen. ⚠️ After Resize() a new buffer is created. The old reference is no longer connected to the canvas - get the buffer again. 🚫 An offset outside the buffer - the Luau error buffer access out of bounds.

chunks.heading: canvas:MarkDirty(x0, y0, x1, y1)
chunks.text: What it does: tells Bloom: "I changed something in this rectangle, send it to the screen". All outcomes: ✅ All tiles touched by the rectangle become dirty. Corners can be given in any order. ✂️ The rectangle is clipped to the canvas. 💤 The rectangle is fully outside the canvas - nothing happens.

chunks.heading: canvas:Resize(resolution)
chunks.text: What it does: changes the canvas size. canvas:Resize(Vector2.new(640, 480)) All outcomes: ✅ Old tiles are deleted, new ones are created. The draft becomes new and fully transparent. The window is reset to the whole canvas. All tiles are dirty. 🧹 Uploads waiting in UpdateAsync are cancelled. 🗑️ The old picture disappears. If you need it, draw it again. 🚫 The canvas was made with FromEditableImage - the error Resize is not supported for contexts created with FromEditableImage. 🚫 Size less than 1 - the error Bloom.Resize expects a positive resolution. 🧠 Not enough memory for the new tiles - a memory budget error. The canvas stays without tiles. Try a smaller size or destroy the canvas. 💤 The canvas is destroyed - nothing happens.

chunks.heading: canvas:Destroy()
chunks.text: What it does: turns the canvas off forever and frees memory. All outcomes: ✅ The scheduler stops, all tasks are cancelled. ✅ Own EditableImage objects and ImageLabel copies are deleted (if the canvas was made with Create). 🔒 If the canvas was made with FromEditableImage, your image and ImageLabel stay. 🔁 Calling it again does nothing. 💤 After destruction Update, Clear, BeginFrame, EndFrame, Resize, DrawTexture, DrawText and ApplyShader do nothing. Lines and shapes still write into the old draft, but it never reaches the screen again. Just do not use a destroyed canvas. Destroy the canvas when you no longer need it, for example when leaving a menu. EditableImage takes a lot of memory, especially on phones. Next: Colors →

chunks.heading: What a color is made of
chunks.text: Every color on screen is mixed from three beams: red (R), green (G) and blue (B). There is also a fourth number - transparency (A, "alpha"). It says how solid the color is. Every number goes from 0 to 255: Number For R, G, B For A (alpha) 0 this beam is off the color is invisible 128 half half transparent 255 full beam the color is fully solid Color R G B Black 0 0 0 White 255 255 255 Red 255 0 0 Green 0 255 0 Blue 0 0 255 Yellow 255 255 0 Purple 128 0 255

chunks.heading: A color as one number
chunks.text: Bloom stores a color as one big number (32 bits). It has 4 slots of 8 bits, and red sits in the lowest one: 0x AA BB GG RR │ │ │ └── red (bits 0–7) │ │ └───── green (bits 8–15) │ └──────── blue (bits 16–23) └─────────── alpha (bits 24–31) For example, solid red is 0xFF0000FF. The bytes lie in the same order in EditableImage:ReadPixelsBuffer(), so Bloom does not reorder anything and works fast. You do not have to remember the byte order. Just use Color4.New32Bit(r, g, b, a).

chunks.heading: Bloom.GetColor4()
chunks.text: What it does: gives you the module with color functions. local Color4 = Bloom.GetColor4() All outcomes: ✅ always returns the same module.

chunks.heading: Color4.New32Bit(R, G, B, A?)
chunks.text: What it does: packs a color number from four parts. Name Type What it is R, G, B number Red, green, blue (0–255) A number? Transparency (0–255). If you do not pass it, it is 255 (fully solid) local orange = Color4.New32Bit(255, 140, 0) local glass = Color4.New32Bit(200, 230, 255, 100) All outcomes: ✅ Returns a color number. ✂️ A number above 255 or below 0 is "cut by a mask": only its lowest 8 bits are kept. For example, 256 becomes 0, and 300 becomes 44. To get "at most 255", use math.clamp first. ✂️ A fractional number is rounded down, because that is how bit32 works.

chunks.heading: Color4.Unpack(color)
chunks.text: What it does: splits a color number back into 4 parts. local r, g, b, a = Color4.Unpack(orange) Returns: r, g, b, a - four numbers from 0 to 255. All outcomes: ✅ always four numbers.

chunks.heading: Color4.SetR(color, value), Color4.SetG(color, value), Color4.SetB(color, value), Color4.SetA(color, value)
chunks.text: What it does: changes one part of a color and returns a new number. The old number does not change. local halfOrange = Color4.SetA(orange, 128) All outcomes: ✅ Returns a new color. ✂️ A value outside 0–255 is cut by a mask, like in New32Bit: only its lowest 8 bits are kept. Pass a whole number from 0 to 255.

chunks.heading: Color4.BlendOver(destination, source)
chunks.text: What it does: puts the color source on top of the color destination, like a piece of colored glass over a drawing. It takes the transparency of both colors into account. local result = Color4.BlendOver( Color4.New32Bit(0, 0, 255), Color4.New32Bit(255, 0, 0, 128) ) All outcomes: ✅ source is fully solid (A = 255) - the result equals source. ✅ source is fully invisible (A = 0) - the result equals destination. ✅ Otherwise the colors are mixed. The more solid source is, the more of it is in the result. ✅ Both colors are invisible - the result is 0. Bloom uses "straight" alpha, not "premultiplied" alpha. The color is stored as is, and alpha sits next to it separately.

chunks.heading: Color4.Zero
chunks.text: This is just the number 0 - fully transparent black.

chunks.heading: Color objects
chunks.text: Sometimes it is handier to work with an object that has the fields R, G, B and A.

chunks.heading: Color4.New(R, G, B, A?)
chunks.text: What it does: creates a color object. local sky = Color4.New(135, 206, 235) print(sky.R, sky.G, sky.B, sky.A) All outcomes: ✅ Numbers are rounded to the nearest whole number and clamped to 0–255. So 300 becomes 255, and −5 becomes 0. The object is safer than New32Bit. ✅ A is 255 by default.

chunks.heading: color:To32Bit()
chunks.text: What it does: turns the object into a color number for drawing functions. canvas:Clear(sky:To32Bit())

chunks.heading: Color4.From32Bit(color)
chunks.text: What it does: turns a color number back into an object.

chunks.heading: Color4.FromColor3(color, alpha?)
chunks.text: What it does: turns a regular Roblox Color3 (parts from 0 to 1) into a Color4 object. local c = Color4.FromColor3(Color3.fromRGB(255, 100, 0)) All outcomes: ✅ parts are multiplied by 255 and rounded. alpha is 255 by default.

chunks.heading: color:Lerp(other, t)
chunks.text: What it does: finds a color "between" two colors. t = 0 is the first color, t = 1 is the second, t = 0.5 is exactly in the middle. local red = Color4.New(255, 0, 0) local blue = Color4.New(0, 0, 255) for x = 1, 100 do local mix = red:Lerp(blue, (x - 1) / 99) canvas:DrawVerticalLine(x, 1, 20, mix:To32Bit()) end All outcomes: ✅ Returns a new color object. ✂️ t below 0 counts as 0, above 1 counts as 1.

chunks.heading: Important: drawing replaces the color
chunks.text: DrawPixel, DrawLine, DrawHorizontalLine, DrawVerticalLine, DrawRectangle and DrawTriangle replace the pixel completely, transparency included. A half-transparent rectangle does not mix with the background - it makes a hole. Only DrawLineAA, DrawTexture (by default) and DrawText mix colors. For everything else use Color4.BlendOver yourself. Next: Drawing →

chunks.heading: Drawing
chunks.text: Here are all of Bloom's "pencils": a dot, lines, a rectangle and a triangle.

chunks.heading: Rules for everything
chunks.text: Counting from one. The top-left pixel is (1, 1), the bottom-right is (canvas.res_x, canvas.res_y). Edges are included. DrawRectangle(1, 1, 3, 3, ...) paints a 3 × 3 square, that is 9 pixels. Order does not matter. (10, 10, 1, 1) draws the same as (1, 1, 10, 10). Going past the edge is fine. Everything that sticks out of the canvas or the window (SetViewport) is simply clipped. There is no error. The color is replaced. All functions here, except DrawLineAA, put the color as is, transparency included, and mix nothing. Tiles get dirty by themselves. Bloom marks the changed places, and after Update() they appear on screen.

chunks.heading: canvas:DrawPixel(x, y, color)
chunks.text: What it does: paints one square. Name Type What it is x number Column number, from 1 y number Row number, from 1 color number A color from Color4.New32Bit canvas:DrawPixel(10, 20, Color4.New32Bit(255, 0, 0)) All outcomes: ✅ The pixel is painted, its tile becomes dirty. ✂️ Fractional coordinates are rounded down: (10.9, 20.2) → (10, 20). 🙈 The dot is outside the canvas or the window - nothing happens, no error. If you need to paint many pixels in a row, DrawRectangle and DrawHorizontalLine are dozens of times faster than thousands of DrawPixel calls.

chunks.heading: canvas:ReadPixel(x, y)
chunks.text: What it does: finds out the color of a square in the draft. Returns: number - the color. You can split it into parts with Color4.Unpack. local color = canvas:ReadPixel(10, 20) local r, g, b, a = Color4.Unpack(color) All outcomes: ✅ Returns the color from the draft, even if it has not been sent to the screen yet. ✂️ Fractional coordinates are rounded down. 0️⃣ The dot is outside the canvas - returns 0. ℹ️ The window (SetViewport) is ignored: you can read anywhere.

chunks.heading: canvas:DrawPixelUnsafe(x, y, color)
chunks.text: What it does: the same as DrawPixel, but without checks. It is faster, but more dangerous. All outcomes: ✅ Whole coordinates inside the canvas - the pixel is painted. 🚫 No rounding, no window, no edge check. 💥 x is bigger than the width - the pixel lands at the start of the next row, not outside the edge. 💥 The dot is completely outside the draft - the error buffer access out of bounds. 💥 Fractional coordinates - the pixel may land in the wrong place. The tile may also be marked wrongly. Use this function only when you are sure about the coordinates, for example in your own loop for x = 1, canvas.res_x.

chunks.heading: canvas:ReadPixelUnsafe(x, y)
chunks.text: What it does: reads a pixel without checks. All outcomes: ✅ correct coordinates - the color. 💥 Wrong ones - someone else's pixel or the error buffer access out of bounds.

chunks.heading: canvas:DrawLine(x0, y0, x1, y1, color)
chunks.text: What it does: draws a thin line, 1 pixel thick, from the point (x0, y0) to the point (x1, y1). canvas:DrawLine(1, 1, 100, 50, Color4.New32Bit(255, 255, 255)) ■ ■ . . . . . . . . ■ ■ . . . . . . . . ■ ■ . . . . . . . . ■ ■ All outcomes: ✅ Both end points are painted. The line goes between them in "steps" (this is Bresenham's algorithm). ✂️ Fractional ends are rounded to the nearest whole number: 2.5 → 3, 2.4 → 2. ✂️ The part of the line outside the window is cut off in advance, so even a very long line is drawn fast. 🙈 The line is completely outside the window - nothing happens. 🔹 Start and end are the same - one dot is drawn.

chunks.heading: canvas:DrawLineAA(x0, y0, x1, y1, thickness, color)
chunks.text: What it does: draws a thick soft line, like a felt-tip pen. Its edges are half transparent and blend smoothly with the background. Name Type What it is thickness number Thickness in pixels color number The color. Its alpha is taken into account too canvas:DrawLineAA(20, 20, 200, 120, 6, Color4.New32Bit(255, 80, 160)) All outcomes: ✅ A round brush with radius floor(thickness / 2) is "stamped" along the line. The middle is solid, the edges are soft. ✅ Every pixel is blended once, using the most solid stamp, so there are no dark stripes at the joints. ✅ A half-transparent color (A < 255) gives a half-transparent line. 🔹 thickness below 2 - the radius is 0, and the line is 1 pixel thick. ✂️ The part outside the window is clipped. 🙈 The line is completely outside the window - nothing happens. 🐢 This is slower than DrawLine: the thicker the line, the more work. This is a brush, not "real" mathematical anti-aliasing. It looks good for interfaces and painting, but it is not suited for very precise graphics.

chunks.heading: canvas:DrawHorizontalLine(x0, y, x1, color)
chunks.text: What it does: draws a straight horizontal line on row y from x0 to x1. canvas:DrawHorizontalLine(1, 50, canvas.res_x, Color4.New32Bit(0, 0, 0)) All outcomes: ✅ All pixels from x0 to x1 inclusive are painted, in any order. ✂️ Numbers are rounded down. ✂️ The line is clipped by the window. 🙈 Row y is outside the window - nothing happens.

chunks.heading: canvas:DrawVerticalLine(x, y0, y1, color)
chunks.text: What it does: draws a straight vertical line in column x from y0 to y1. All outcomes: the same as for the horizontal line, only vertical.

chunks.heading: canvas:DrawRectangle(x0, y0, x1, y1, color)
chunks.text: What it does: draws a filled rectangle. (x0, y0) and (x1, y1) are two opposite corners. canvas:DrawRectangle(10, 10, 60, 40, Color4.New32Bit(40, 180, 255)) All outcomes: ✅ Everything is painted, edges included. ✂️ Corners are rounded down, order does not matter. ✂️ The rectangle is clipped by the window. 🙈 Completely outside the window - nothing happens. ⚡ Very fast: one row is prepared once and copied whole. How to draw just a frame (without filling): local function drawFrame(canvas, x0, y0, x1, y1, color) canvas:DrawHorizontalLine(x0, y0, x1, color) canvas:DrawHorizontalLine(x0, y1, x1, color) canvas:DrawVerticalLine(x0, y0, y1, color) canvas:DrawVerticalLine(x1, y0, y1, color) end

chunks.heading: canvas:DrawTriangle(x0, y0, x1, y1, x2, y2, color)
chunks.text: What it does: draws a filled triangle from three corners. canvas:DrawTriangle(50, 10, 10, 90, 90, 90, Color4.New32Bit(255, 200, 0)) ▲ (50, 10) ███ █████ ███████ (10, 90) (90, 90) All outcomes: ✅ The triangle is filled row by row from top to bottom. Corners can be given in any order. ✂️ Corners are rounded down, and row edges to the nearest whole number. 🔹 All three corners are on one row - a horizontal line is drawn. 🔹 All three corners are on one straight line - a thin strip along it is drawn. ✂️ Clipped by the window. How to draw a polygon: cut it into triangles like a "fan" from the first corner: local function drawPolygon(canvas, points, color) for i = 2, #points - 1 do local a, b, c = points[1], points[i], points[i + 1] canvas:DrawTriangle(a.X, a.Y, b.X, b.Y, c.X, c.Y, color) end end This works for convex shapes: squares, hexagons, circles made of many points.

chunks.heading: Recipe: a circle
chunks.text: There is no separate circle function, but it is easy to build one from horizontal lines: local function drawCircle(canvas, cx, cy, radius, color) for dy = -radius, radius do local half = math.floor(math.sqrt(radius * radius - dy * dy)) canvas:DrawHorizontalLine(cx - half, cy + dy, cx + half, color) end end drawCircle(canvas, 100, 100, 30, Color4.New32Bit(255, 220, 0)) Next: Textures →

chunks.heading: Textures
chunks.text: A texture is a ready-made picture that lives in memory, like a sticker in an album. You can "stick" it onto the canvas many times: anywhere, at any size, with a tint and transparency. texture 4×2 canvas ┌──────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ │ ▓▓░░ │ Draw → │ ▓▓▓▓░░░░ │ │ ▓▓░░ │ ×2 size │ ▓▓▓▓░░░░ │ └──────┘ │ ▓▓▓▓░░░░ │ │ ▓▓▓▓░░░░ │ └──────────────────┘ Textures live in the Bloom.Texture module. local Texture = Bloom.Texture

chunks.heading: Texture.New(width, height, pixels, copy_pixels?)
chunks.text: What it does: makes a texture from your own pixel buffer. Name Type What it is width, height number Size in pixels (rounded down) pixels buffer Exactly width * height * 4 bytes: R, G, B, A for every pixel, row after row copy_pixels boolean? By default the buffer is copied. false - use your buffer without a copy local pixels = buffer.create(2 * 2 * 4) buffer.writeu32(pixels, 0, Color4.New32Bit(255, 0, 0)) buffer.writeu32(pixels, 4, Color4.New32Bit(0, 255, 0)) buffer.writeu32(pixels, 8, Color4.New32Bit(0, 0, 255)) buffer.writeu32(pixels, 12, Color4.New32Bit(255, 255, 255)) local checker = Texture.New(2, 2, pixels) All outcomes: ✅ The texture is created. 📋 copy_pixels is not given or is true - the texture has its own copy, and you can keep changing your buffer safely. 🔗 copy_pixels = false - the texture uses your buffer. If you change it, the texture changes too. This saves memory. 🚫 Width or height less than 1 - the error Texture.New expects positive dimensions. 🚫 The buffer size is not width * height * 4 - the error Texture.New expects width * height * 4 RGBA bytes.

chunks.heading: Texture.FromEditableImage(editable_image)
chunks.text: What it does: copies the pixels of an EditableImage into a new texture. local tex = Texture.FromEditableImage(myEditableImage) All outcomes: ✅ A texture of the same size as the image. 🔒 The image itself is not changed or deleted. ℹ️ If you change the image later, the texture stays old: it is a copy.

chunks.heading: Texture.FromContent(content)
chunks.text: What it does: loads a picture from Roblox (for example by rbxassetid://) and makes a texture from it. This function waits for loading (it yields). Do not call it inside RenderStepped - call it in advance, at startup. local tex = Texture.FromContent(Content.fromUri("rbxassetid://1234567890")) All outcomes: ✅ The picture loaded - the texture is ready. The temporary EditableImage is deleted right away. 🚫 The picture is not yours (Roblox only allows loading pictures of the game's creator or group) - an error from Roblox. 🚫 Allow Mesh / Image APIs is off - an error from Roblox. 🧠 Out of memory - the error Texture.FromContent: EditableImage memory budget is exhausted. 🚫 The pixels could not be read - the error is passed on, and the temporary image is deleted anyway.

chunks.heading: texture:GetPixel(x, y)
chunks.text: What it does: finds out the color of a texture pixel. Coordinates start from 1, as everywhere. All outcomes: ✅ Returns the color. ✂️ Fractional coordinates are rounded down. 0️⃣ Outside the texture - 0. 0️⃣ The texture is destroyed - 0.

chunks.heading: texture:Destroy()
chunks.text: What it does: frees the texture's memory. All outcomes: ✅ The buffer is replaced with an empty one, texture.destroyed = true. 🚫 A destroyed texture cannot be drawn: you get the error Cannot draw a destroyed Texture. 🔁 Calling it again is safe.

chunks.heading: Texture fields
chunks.text: Field What it is texture.width, texture.height Size texture.pixels Pixel buffer texture.destroyed true if the texture is destroyed

chunks.heading: canvas:DrawTexture(texture, x, y, width?, height?, options?)
chunks.text: What it does: puts the texture onto the canvas. Name Type What it is texture Texture What to draw x, y number Where the top-left corner goes width, height number? What size to draw. By default - the texture's size options DrawOptions? Extra settings (see the table below) options settings: Field Default What it does source_x, source_y 1, 1 Where in the texture to start cutting a piece source_width, source_height the whole texture What size of piece to cut tint white 0xFFFFFFFF Tint: every channel is multiplied by the channel of this color opacity 1 Transparency from 0 (invisible) to 1 (as is) blend true true - mix with the background by transparency. false - just replace the pixels Examples: canvas:DrawTexture(tex, 10, 10) canvas:DrawTexture(tex, 10, 10, tex.width * 3, tex.height * 3) canvas:DrawTexture(tex, 50, 50, nil, nil, { tint = Color4.New32Bit(255, 120, 120), opacity = 0.5, }) canvas:DrawTexture(spriteSheet, 100, 100, 32, 32, { source_x = 33, source_y = 1, source_width = 32, source_height = 32, }) The last example is a sprite sheet: one big picture with many frames. A 32 × 32 frame starting at pixel 33 is cut out of it. All outcomes: ✅ The texture is drawn. Stretching and shrinking use "nearest neighbor": pixels become little squares, without blur. That is exactly right for pixel art. ✂️ Coordinates and sizes are rounded down. ✂️ The source_* piece is clamped inside the texture: it cannot go past the edge. ✂️ The result is clipped by the canvas and the window. 🎨 tint is white and opacity = 1 - pixels are not recolored, and drawing is faster. 🎨 opacity below 0 counts as 0, above 1 counts as 1. 🧱 blend = false - pixels are replaced completely, transparency included. This is the fastest mode for opaque pictures. 🙈 width or height is 0 or less - nothing happens. 🙈 The place is completely outside the canvas - nothing happens. 💤 The canvas is destroyed - nothing happens. 🚫 The texture is destroyed - the error Cannot draw a destroyed Texture. Create textures once at startup, and only draw them every frame. Creating a texture copies a lot of memory. Next: Shaders →

chunks.heading: Shaders
chunks.text: A shader is a magic filter. You give it a piece of the canvas, and it looks at every pixel in turn and decides what that pixel becomes. It is like phone camera filters: "black and white", "brighter", "inverted". before: ▓▓░░▒▒ → Invert → after: ░░▓▓▒▒ Bloom shaders run on the processor, not on the graphics card. A shader over a whole 1024 × 1024 canvas calls your function more than a million times. Apply shaders to small pieces and not every frame. Shaders live in Bloom.Shader. local Shader = Bloom.Shader

chunks.heading: Shader.Invert()
chunks.text: What it does: turns colors inside out: black becomes white, red becomes cyan. Transparency does not change. canvas:ApplyShader(Shader.Invert(), 1, 1, canvas.res_x, canvas.res_y)

chunks.heading: Shader.Grayscale()
chunks.text: What it does: makes the picture black and white. Brightness is calculated the way the eye sees it (the Rec. 709 formula): green looks brighter than blue. Transparency does not change.

chunks.heading: Shader.Brightness(amount?)
chunks.text: What it does: makes things brighter or darker. amount = 1 - as it was, 2 - twice as bright, 0.5 - darker, 0 - black. local bright = Shader.Brightness(1.3) canvas:ApplyShader(bright, 1, 1, 100, 100) canvas:ApplyShader(bright, 1, 1, 100, 100, { amount = 0.7 }) All outcomes: ✅ Every channel is multiplied by amount and capped at 255. 🔹 amount is not given - it is 1. 🔹 amount below 0 counts as 0. 🔹 uniforms holds something other than a number - 1 is used.

chunks.heading: Bloom.CreateShader(name, callback, uniforms?)
chunks.text: This is the same as Shader.New(name, callback, uniforms?). What it does: creates your own filter. Name Type What it is name string A name so you do not get confused (not empty) callback function A function called for every pixel uniforms table? Default settings that the function receives The callback function receives: Argument What it is x, y Where the pixel is on the canvas (from 1) u, v Where the pixel is inside the piece: from 0 (left/top edge) to 1 (right/bottom edge) color32 The pixel's current color uniforms Settings And must return: a new color (number) or nil if the pixel should not change. local gradient = Bloom.CreateShader("Gradient", function(x, y, u, v, color32, uniforms) local red = math.floor(u * 255) local blue = math.floor(v * 255) return Color4.New32Bit(red, 0, blue, 255) end) canvas:ApplyShader(gradient, 1, 1, 200, 200) local threshold = Bloom.CreateShader("Threshold", function(_, _, _, _, color32, uniforms) local r, g, b, a = Color4.Unpack(color32) local value = if (r + g + b) / 3 >= uniforms.level then 255 else 0 return Color4.New32Bit(value, value, value, a) end, { level = 128 }) All outcomes when creating: ✅ Returns a shader { name, callback, uniforms, enabled = true }. 🚫 name is not a string or is empty - the error Shader.New expects a name. 🚫 callback is not a function - the error Shader.New expects a callback. How to turn a shader off without deleting it: myShader.enabled = false. After that ApplyShader skips it.

chunks.heading: canvas:ApplyShader(shader, x0, y0, x1, y1, uniforms?)
chunks.text: What it does: runs a rectangle of the canvas through the shader. Name Type What it is shader Shader Which filter x0, y0, x1, y1 number Rectangle corners (inclusive, in any order) uniforms table? Settings for this call. If given, they fully replace the shader's settings Returns: number - how many pixels were processed. All outcomes: ✅ Every pixel went through the function. The number of pixels is returned. 🎬 The beforeShader stage runs before the work, afterShader after it. 🔹 The function returned nil - the pixel stayed the same. ✂️ The rectangle is clipped by the canvas and the window. 0️⃣ The rectangle is completely outside the window - returns 0, and the stages do not run. 0️⃣ shader.enabled = false - returns 0. 0️⃣ The canvas is destroyed - returns 0. 📏 A rectangle 1 pixel wide - u is always 0. 1 pixel tall - v is always 0. 💥 The function raised an error - the error flies out of ApplyShader. Pixels processed so far are already changed, and the tiles are marked dirty. The afterShader stage does not run. 💥 The function returned something that is not a number (for example a string) - a Luau error when writing to the buffer.

chunks.heading: How to make a shader fast
chunks.text: Create nothing inside the function: no {}, Vector2.new, Color3.new, function() end. Create everything you need outside. Apply it to a small piece. Need to darken a button - take the button's rectangle, not the whole screen. Do not apply it every frame if the picture does not change. Return nil for pixels that do not change: fewer writes to memory. local function slow(_, _, _, _, color32) local parts = { Color4.Unpack(color32) } return Color4.New32Bit(parts[1], parts[2], parts[3], parts[4]) end local function fast(_, _, _, _, color32) local r, g, b, a = Color4.Unpack(color32) return Color4.New32Bit(r, g, b, a) end Next: Fonts and text →

chunks.heading: Fonts and text
chunks.text: To write letters on the canvas, Bloom needs a font. A font in Bloom is a cheat-sheet picture with all the letters drawn on it (it is called an atlas), plus a table saying where each letter is on that picture. atlas: ┌───┬───┬───┬───┬───┐ │ A │ B │ C │ D │ … │ DrawText("CAB") → take C, then A, then B └───┴───┴───┴───┴───┘ and stick them in order Fonts live in Bloom.Font. local Font = Bloom.Font

chunks.heading: Way 1. From a .ttf file
chunks.text: Bloom can read TrueType font files (.ttf) by itself and draw an atlas from them.

chunks.heading: Font.FromString(font_data, pixel_size, charset?, options?)
chunks.text: What it does: turns the bytes of a .ttf file (as a string) into a font. Name Type What it is font_data string The raw bytes of the .ttf file. Not Base64, but the bytes themselves pixel_size number Letter size in pixels, from 4 to 128 charset string? Which letters to prepare. By default - all printable ASCII characters (English letters, digits and signs) options Options? spacing - extra space between letters, fallback - the code of the replacement letter (? by default) local font = Font.FromString(fontBytes, 18) local russian = Font.FromString(fontBytes, 16, " АБВГДЕЁЖЗИЙКЛМНОПРСТУФХЦЧШЩЪЫЬЭЮЯабвгдеёжзийклмнопрстуфхцчшщъыьэюя0123456789.,!?-" ) All outcomes: ✅ The font is ready. Letters are drawn white with soft edges, so you can tint them any color. ✅ The ? letter is always added, even if it is not in charset: it is needed as a replacement for unknown letters. ✅ Repeated letters in charset do no harm: each one is prepared once. 🔤 Cyrillic and other letters work if they exist in the font itself and in charset. charset is written in UTF-8, like a regular Luau string. 🚫 The string is shorter than 12 bytes or not a string at all - the error Font.FromString expects a non-empty binary font string. 🚫 pixel_size is below 4 or above 128 - the error Font.FromBuffer pixel_size must be between 4 and 128. 🚫 It is not TrueType (for example .otf with CFF, .woff, .woff2) - the error Font supports TrueType-outline TTF files only; CFF/WOFF/WOFF2 are not supported. 🚫 The file lacks required tables - the error TTF is missing a required TrueType table. 🚫 There is no Unicode table (cmap format 4 or 12) - the error TTF has no supported Unicode cmap (format 4 or 12). 🚫 The file is cut or broken - the error Invalid or truncated TrueType font: .... 🚫 Strange font sizes - the error Invalid TrueType metrics. 🚫 Too many letters or too big a size (the atlas is bigger than 1024 × 1024) - the error Font atlas is too large; reduce pixel_size or the charset. 🔹 If a letter from charset does not exist in the font itself, the font's "unknown" sign goes into the atlas instead. Usually it is an empty box. FromString is heavy work: every letter has to be drawn from curves. Do it once at startup, not every frame. Not supported: CFF fonts (usually .otf), WOFF and WOFF2, variable fonts and composite letters attached by points. Convert such a font into a regular static .ttf first, for example in FontForge.

chunks.heading: Font.FromBuffer(font_buffer, pixel_size, charset?, options?)
chunks.text: What it does: the same, but the bytes are in a buffer, not in a string. All outcomes: the same as for FromString. If the buffer is shorter than 12 bytes - the error Font.FromBuffer expects a non-empty binary font buffer.

chunks.heading: How to get .ttf bytes into Roblox
Way 2. Your own atlas
chunks.text: If you already have a picture with all the letters (for example a pixel font), make the font yourself.

chunks.heading: Font.New(atlas, glyphs, line_height, options?)
chunks.text: Name Type What it is atlas Texture The picture with all the letters glyphs table Where each letter is. The key is the letter itself ("A") or its code (65) line_height number Line height in pixels options Options? spacing and fallback Every letter (glyph) is described like this: Field Required? What it is x, y yes Top-left corner of the letter in the atlas (from 1) width, height yes Letter size in the atlas xoffset no How far to shift the letter right when drawing yoffset no How far to shift the letter down from the top of the line xadvance no How far to step right after the letter. By default - width local atlas = Bloom.Texture.FromEditableImage(fontImage) local pixelFont = Font.New(atlas, { A = { x = 1, y = 1, width = 5, height = 7, xadvance = 6 }, B = { x = 7, y = 1, width = 5, height = 7, xadvance = 6 }, [" "] = { x = 1, y = 1, width = 0, height = 0, xadvance = 4 }, ["?"] = { x = 13, y = 1, width = 5, height = 7, xadvance = 6 }, }, 8) All outcomes: ✅ The font is created. Letter keys are turned into codes. If a key is a string of several letters, only the first one is used. ✅ line_height is rounded down. 🚫 The atlas is already destroyed - the error Font.New expects a live texture atlas. 🚫 line_height is 0 or less - the error Font.New expects a positive line height. 🔗 The atlas now belongs to the font: font:Destroy() destroys it too.

chunks.heading: canvas:DrawText(font, text, x, y, color?, scale?)
chunks.text: What it does: writes text on the canvas. Name Type What it is font Font Which font text string What to write (UTF-8) x, y number Top-left corner of the text color number? Color. White by default scale number? Zoom. 2 - twice as big. 1 by default Returns: width, height - how much space the text took in pixels. local w, h = canvas:DrawText(font, "Hello!\nSecond line", 10, 10, Color4.New32Bit(255, 220, 0), 2) All outcomes: ✅ The text is drawn and blended with the background by transparency. ↩️ \n - a new line. ⇥ \t - an indent 4 spaces wide. ❓ The letter is not in the font - the replacement letter is drawn (fallback, ? by default). 🙈 Neither the letter nor the replacement exists - the letter is skipped, with no space for it. 📏 Scaling enlarges letters with "nearest neighbor": with scale = 2 every pixel becomes a 2 × 2 square. ✂️ Text past the edge of the canvas or the window is clipped. 0️⃣ The canvas or the font is destroyed - nothing is drawn, 0, 0 is returned. 🚫 text is not a string (for example a number) - the error DrawText expects a string. Use tostring(number). 🚫 scale is 0 or less - the error DrawText expects a positive scale. 🚫 The string has broken UTF-8 - a Luau error from utf8.codes.

chunks.heading: Font.MeasureText(font, text, scale?)
chunks.text: What it does: finds out the text size without drawing it. The rules are the same as in DrawText. Returns: width, height. local w, h = Font.MeasureText(font, "Play", 2) local x = math.floor((canvas.res_x - w) / 2) + 1 canvas:DrawText(font, "Play", x, 50, nil, 2) This puts the text exactly in the center. All outcomes: ✅ Returns the size. Height = number of lines × line height × scale. ℹ️ Width is counted by letter steps (xadvance), so it can be a pixel or two wider than the visible letters.

chunks.heading: font:Destroy()
chunks.text: What it does: destroys the font's atlas. All outcomes: ✅ the atlas is destroyed, and DrawText with this font draws nothing anymore. 🔁 Calling it again is safe.

chunks.heading: Font fields
chunks.text: Field What it is font.texture The atlas font.glyphs Letters (code → glyph) font.line_height Line height font.spacing Extra space between letters font.fallback Code of the replacement letter font.destroyed true if the font is destroyed Next: Task scheduler →

chunks.heading: Task scheduler
chunks.text: Imagine you have lots of chores. If you do everything at once, you get tired and finish nothing. It is better to do a little at a time: a bit now, a bit later. The most important chores first. The scheduler (Async) works just like that. It does tasks in small portions and makes sure every portion fits into a budget - a few milliseconds. So the game does not freeze. queue: [urgent!] [normal] [normal] [background] ... │ step Step() - work for ≤ budget seconds ▼ done ✓ Every canvas has its own scheduler: canvas.async. You can also make a separate one: Bloom.Async.New().

chunks.heading: Priorities
chunks.text: Priority Meaning 0 Most urgent 1 Normal (default) 2 Not urgent 3 Background, when there is nothing else to do Within one priority, tasks go in turn: first come, first served. Aging. A task that waits a long time becomes more important: every aging_interval seconds (0.25 by default) it moves up one level. So background tasks eventually run too. Deadline. If a task's deadline has passed, it jumps ahead of all regular priorities.

chunks.heading: Bloom.Async.New(budget?, options?)
chunks.text: What it does: creates a new scheduler. Name Default What it is budget 0.002 Seconds per step (minimum 0.0001) options.poll_interval 0.001 Pause between steps in Start(), in seconds options.aging_interval 0.25 After how many seconds of waiting a task becomes more important options.max_tasks_per_step 256 Maximum tasks per step (minimum 1) local scheduler = Bloom.Async.New(0.001, { max_tasks_per_step = 64 }) For a canvas these settings are set in Bloom.Create through async_budget and scheduler_options.

chunks.heading: scheduler:Submit(callback, ...)
chunks.text: What it does: puts a task into the queue with normal priority. All arguments after the function are passed to it. local job = canvas.async:Submit(function(name, count) print(name, count) end, "hello", 3) Returns: a task (Task). All outcomes: ✅ The task is in the queue with the status "pending". ⏸️ It does not start by itself. You need to call scheduler:Start() or scheduler:Step(). 🚫 callback is not a function - the error Async.Submit expects a function.

chunks.heading: scheduler:SubmitWithOptions(callback, options, ...)
chunks.text: What it does: the same, but with a priority and/or a deadline. options field What it is priority From 0 to 3. The number is rounded down and clamped to these limits deadline The deadline - an absolute os.clock() time, not "in how many seconds" canvas.async:SubmitWithOptions(function() print("urgent!") end, { priority = 0, deadline = os.clock() + 0.05 })

chunks.heading: canvas:Submit(callback, ...) and canvas:SubmitWithOptions(callback, options, ...)
chunks.text: These are short versions of canvas.async:Submit and canvas.async:SubmitWithOptions.

chunks.heading: scheduler:Start()
chunks.text: What it does: starts a background loop. It calls Step() by itself, waits poll_interval and repeats. All outcomes: ✅ Tasks start running by themselves. 🔁 The loop is already running - nothing happens. ℹ️ The loop is built on task.spawn and task.wait and does not connect to RenderStepped or Heartbeat. ℹ️ When tasks run out, the loop keeps quietly spinning and waiting for new ones. You can stop it with Stop().

chunks.heading: scheduler:Stop()
chunks.text: What it does: stops the background loop. Tasks stay in the queue, and you can continue them with Start() or Step().

chunks.heading: scheduler:Step(budget?)
chunks.text: What it does: runs tasks once, right now, until the budget runs out. Returns: number - how many tasks were started or continued. RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function() canvas.async:Step(0.001) end) All outcomes: ✅ Tasks run by priority. ⏱️ The budget is checked between tasks. The first task always runs, even if it is long. 🛑 At most max_tasks_per_step tasks run in one step. 0️⃣ The queue is empty - returns 0.

chunks.heading: Long tasks and pauses
chunks.text: The scheduler cannot stop a task in the middle of its work. If a task is long, split it into pieces and say "I'll wait" between them.

chunks.heading: Bloom.Async.Yield()
chunks.text: What it does: pauses the current task and lets other tasks run. The task goes back into the queue and later continues from the same place. canvas.async:Submit(function() for row = 1, canvas.res_y do canvas:DrawHorizontalLine(1, row, canvas.res_x, Color4.New32Bit(row % 256, 0, 0)) if row % 32 == 0 then Bloom.Async.Yield() end end canvas:Update() end) canvas.async:Start() All outcomes: ✅ Inside a task - a pause, and the task gets the status "yielded". 🚫 Outside a task - the error Async.Yield must be called from inside a scheduler task. Inside a task you must not use task.wait(), wait() and other Roblox waits (for example :WaitForChild() or HttpService:GetAsync()). The task immediately becomes "failed" with the error Task yielded outside Async.Yield(); .... For pauses use only Bloom.Async.Yield().

chunks.heading: Task
chunks.text: Field What it is job.state Status (see the table below) job.priority Priority job.submitted_at, job.started_at, job.finished_at Time by os.clock() job.deadline Deadline job.error Error text, if the task failed Status Meaning "pending" Waiting in the queue "running" Running right now "yielded" Paused after Yield(), waiting to continue "completed" Done ✓ "cancelled" Cancelled ✗ "failed" Failed with an error 💥

chunks.heading: job:Cancel()
chunks.text: What it does: cancels the task. All outcomes: ✅ The task is waiting (pending) or paused (yielded) - it becomes "cancelled" and does not run. 💤 The task is already done, failed or cancelled - nothing happens. ⚠️ The task is running right now - it cannot be cancelled.

chunks.heading: job:IsCancelled() and job:IsFinished()
chunks.text: What it does: quickly tells whether the task is cancelled and whether it has ended. IsCancelled() → true if the status is "cancelled". IsFinished() → true if the status is "completed", "cancelled" or "failed".

chunks.heading: Errors in tasks
chunks.text: If a task raises an error: ✅ The scheduler does not break and runs the other tasks. 📝 The task gets state = "failed", and job.error holds the error text. ⚠️ The console shows [Bloom.Async] Task failed: ....

chunks.heading: scheduler:Clear()
chunks.text: What it does: cancels all tasks in the queue. All outcomes: ✅ all waiting and paused tasks become "cancelled". ⚠️ A task that is running right now stops only at its next Yield().

chunks.heading: scheduler:PendingCount()
chunks.text: Returns: how many tasks are waiting or paused.

chunks.heading: scheduler:GetStats()
chunks.text: Returns: a copy of the counters. Field What it is pending Waiting active Running now completed Done in total failed Failed in total cancelled Cancelled in total last_step_seconds How long the last step took max_step_seconds The longest step

chunks.heading: scheduler:Destroy()
chunks.text: What it does: Stop() and Clear() together. canvas:Destroy() calls it by itself. The scheduler does not make work parallel on several cores. It only shares time fairly. Do not draw on one canvas from different Actors at the same time. Next: Stage pipeline →

chunks.heading: Stage pipeline
chunks.text: Imagine a conveyor belt in a toy factory. A toy rides along the belt, and workers stand at the right spots: one paints, another glues, a third packs. In Bloom the frame rides along such a belt, and the stages are the workers. You can put your own worker in the right spot and do something at the right moment. BeginFrame ─► [beginFrame] ─► drawing ─► [beforeShader]→shader→[afterShader] │ EndFrame ─► [endFrame] ─► [beforeUpload] ─► tiles ─► [tileUploaded]… ─► [afterUpload]

chunks.heading: Phases
chunks.text: Phase When it runs "beginFrame" In BeginFrame(), after filling "endFrame" At the start of EndFrame() "beforeUpload" At the start of Update() and UpdateAsync() "tileUploaded" After every tile sent with UpdateAsync() "afterUpload" When everything is sent "beforeShader" Before every ApplyShader() "afterShader" After every ApplyShader()

chunks.heading: canvas:RegisterStage(name, callback, order?)
chunks.text: What it does: puts your own worker on the belt. It is called in all phases, so check inside which phase is happening now. Name Type What it is name string A unique, non-empty name callback (canvas, phase) -> () What to do order number? Order. Lower runs earlier. 100 by default canvas:RegisterStage("watermark", function(c, phase) if phase == "endFrame" then c:DrawText(font, "demo", c.res_x - 40, c.res_y - 14, Color4.New32Bit(255, 255, 255, 120)) end end, 50) All outcomes: ✅ The stage is added and enabled. 🔁 A stage with this name already exists - it is replaced by the new one. 🔢 Stages with the same order run in alphabetical order of their names. 🚫 An empty name or not a string - the error Pipeline.Register expects a non-empty name. 🚫 callback is not a function - the error Pipeline.Register expects a callback.

chunks.heading: canvas:RemoveStage(name)
chunks.text: Returns: true if the stage existed and was removed. false if there is no such stage.

chunks.heading: canvas.pipeline:SetEnabled(name, enabled)
chunks.text: What it does: temporarily turns a stage off or on without removing it. Returns: true if the stage was found, otherwise false.

chunks.heading: canvas.pipeline:Run(canvas, phase)
chunks.text: What it does: runs all enabled stages for any phase, even your own. canvas.pipeline:Run(canvas, "myCustomPhase")

chunks.heading: What happens if a stage breaks
chunks.text: ✅ The other stages still run. ⚠️ The console shows [Bloom.Pipeline] Stage 'name' failed during 'phase': error text. ✅ A stage can add and remove stages while it runs: the pipeline walks a snapshot of the list. Do not call Update(), EndFrame() or UpdateAsync() inside the beforeUpload, afterUpload and endFrame stages. You get an endless loop. Next: Stats and speed →

chunks.heading: canvas:GetStats()
chunks.text: What it does: gives you a copy of all counters of the canvas and its scheduler. local stats = canvas:GetStats() print(("Uploaded %d tiles, %.1f KB"):format(stats.uploaded_tiles, stats.uploaded_bytes / 1024)) Field What it counts update_calls How many screen updates have finished last_update_seconds How long the last Update() took uploaded_tiles How many tiles were sent to the screen uploaded_bytes How many bytes were sent upload_seconds Total time spent sending shader_pixels How many pixels went through shaders texture_pixels How many pixels were drawn by textures and text text_glyphs How many letters were drawn scheduler_pending Tasks in the queue scheduler_active Tasks running now scheduler_completed Tasks done scheduler_failed Tasks failed scheduler_cancelled Tasks cancelled scheduler_last_step_seconds Length of the last scheduler step scheduler_max_step_seconds The longest scheduler step

chunks.heading: canvas:ResetStats()
chunks.text: What it does: sets the canvas counters to zero. All outcomes: ✅ the fields update_calls … text_glyphs become 0. ⚠️ The scheduler counters (scheduler_*) are not reset: they live in canvas.async.

chunks.heading: Rules for a fast game
chunks.text: Rule Why Keep the canvas small Every pixel is processor work and memory. 512 × 512 is 4 times cheaper than 1024 × 1024 Redraw only what changed Bloom sends only dirty tiles to the screen Use a smaller tile_size for big canvases where small pieces change Then small tiles get dirty, not huge ones Do not make tiles too small Every tile is a separate EditableImage and a separate upload Draw with rectangles and textures, not thousands of DrawPixel One call that fills a whole row is faster than a thousand calls Use blend = false for opaque textures Mixing colors is expensive Apply shaders to small pieces A shader calls a function for every pixel Create fonts, textures and shaders once Creating is expensive, drawing is cheap Use UpdateAsync for big updates The work is spread over frames Destroy unused canvases with Destroy() Phones have little memory for EditableImage

chunks.heading: Roblox limits
chunks.text: One EditableImage is at most 1024 × 1024. Bloom cuts the canvas into tiles by itself. Only one EditableImage is updated on screen per frame. If there are many tiles, the picture updates one tile at a time. Phones have a strict memory limit for EditableImage. If it runs out, Create raises a memory budget error. In a published game you need to turn on Allow Mesh / Image APIs (chapter 2).

chunks.heading: How to find what is slow
chunks.text: Open the MicroProfiler (Ctrl + F6) or the Script Profiler in Studio. Compare canvas:GetStats() before and after the suspicious place. If shader_pixels grows - make the shader smaller. If uploaded_bytes grows - you redraw too much. Next: All errors →

chunks.heading: All errors
chunks.text: Here are all messages Bloom can show. Find yours (Ctrl + F) and read what to do. There are two kinds of messages: 🚫 Error (error) - the script stops. You can catch it with pcall. ⚠️ Warning (warn) - the script keeps working, and a yellow line appears in the console.

chunks.heading: Game settings and memory
chunks.text: Message Kind Why What to do Bloom: EditableImage is not available in this experience. ...Allow Mesh / Image APIs... 🚫 The EditableImage permission is off, or Roblox refused to create or write the image Turn on Allow Mesh / Image APIs (chapter 2). The brackets at the end hold the exact Roblox error Bloom: EditableImage memory budget is exhausted on this device; ... 🚫 The check could not create even a 1 × 1 image Destroy unused canvases and EditableImage objects, make the canvas smaller Bloom: EditableImage memory budget is exhausted (WxH tile) 🚫 Not enough memory for the next tile The same. Bloom already deleted the tiles it created Texture.FromContent: EditableImage memory budget is exhausted 🚫 Not enough memory to load the picture Free memory, load smaller pictures

chunks.text: Message Why What to do buffer access out of bounds DrawPixelUnsafe, ReadPixelUnsafe or a write into GetBuffer() outside the limits Check the coordinates or use the safe functions invalid UTF-8 code Broken UTF-8 in the text for DrawText Check the string attempt to index nil with ... chunks.heading: How to catch an error
chunks.text: local ok, result = pcall(Bloom.Create, Vector2.new(256, 256), frame, template) if ok then local canvas = result canvas:Clear(Color4.New32Bit(0, 0, 0)) canvas:Update() else warn("Could not create the canvas: " .. tostring(result)) end Next: Types →

chunks.heading: Types
chunks.text: Bloom is written in --!strict mode. If you also write in strict mode, Luau points out mistakes before the game starts: for example, if you pass a string instead of a number. Types are checked only while you write code (in Studio or luau-lsp). They do not exist while the game runs. That is why Bloom does real checks (assert) by itself.

chunks.heading: Types from the main module
chunks.text: local Bloom = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.Bloom) type Bloom = Bloom.Bloom type Options = Bloom.Options type Stats = Bloom.Stats type Task = Bloom.Task type SupportReport = Bloom.SupportReport type TextureDrawOptions = Bloom.TextureDrawOptions type FontOptions = Bloom.FontOptions type SchedulerOptions = Bloom.SchedulerOptions type SubmitOptions = Bloom.SubmitOptions type UniformMap = Bloom.UniformMap Type What it is Bloom A canvas Options Bloom.Create settings: tile_size, async_budget, scheduler_options, auto_clip, clear_color Stats The result of GetStats() Task A scheduler task SupportReport The result of CheckSupport(): supported, status, message, details TextureDrawOptions DrawTexture settings FontOptions spacing, fallback SchedulerOptions poll_interval, aging_interval, max_tasks_per_step SubmitOptions priority, deadline UniformMap Shader settings: a table { [string]: value }, where a value is a number, a string, a boolean, a Vector2, a Color3 and other Roblox types

chunks.heading: Example
chunks.text: --!strict local Bloom = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.Bloom) local options: Bloom.Options = { tile_size = 512, clear_color = Bloom.GetColor4().New32Bit(0, 0, 0), } local canvas: Bloom.Bloom = Bloom.Create(Vector2.new(512, 512), frame, template, options) local function drawHud(target: Bloom.Bloom, health: number): () target:DrawRectangle(1, 1, math.floor(health), 8, 0xFF0000FF) end

chunks.heading: Color types
chunks.text: A color is a regular number. In the source code it has the name PackedColor, but it is just a number. Color4.New returns an object of type Color4.Color4, which has the fields R, G, B, A and the methods To32Bit and Lerp.

chunks.heading: Why is nothing visible?
chunks.text: Check in order: Did you call canvas:Update() or canvas:EndFrame()? Did you pass both parent and reference to Bloom.Create? Is parent visible on screen? For example, is the ScreenGui inside PlayerGui? Is the code in a LocalScript, not in a Script? Is the color not transparent? Color4.New32Bit(255, 0, 0, 0) has alpha 0, it is invisible. Is the window not narrowed? Call canvas:ResetViewport().

chunks.heading: Why does the picture update with a delay?
chunks.text: Roblox updates one EditableImage on screen per frame. If the canvas is cut into 4 tiles and all of them changed, a full update takes 4 frames. Make the canvas smaller or raise tile_size (maximum 1024) so there are fewer tiles.

chunks.heading: Why did a half-transparent rectangle make a "hole"?
chunks.text: DrawRectangle replaces pixels instead of mixing them. Draw a half-transparent texture with DrawTexture (it mixes) or mix yourself with Color4.BlendOver.

chunks.heading: Can I draw on the server?
chunks.text: You can: EditableImage can be created on the server too. But players will not see it, because it is not sent over the network. Draw on the client.

chunks.heading: Can I draw on a SurfaceGui (on a part in the world)?
chunks.text: Yes. Pass a SurfaceGui or a Frame inside it as parent. Remember that Bloom gives tiles a size in pixels (UDim2.fromOffset). Set SurfaceGui.PixelsPerStud or SizingMode so the picture has the size you need.

chunks.heading: How do I stretch the picture to the whole screen?
chunks.text: The canvas is always drawn pixel for pixel. To stretch it, put it into a Frame and use UIScale: local scale = Instance.new("UIScale") scale.Scale = 2 scale.Parent = frame For crisp pixels set ResampleMode = Enum.ResamplerMode.Pixelated on reference.

chunks.heading: How many canvases can I create?
chunks.text: As many as memory allows. Every pixel takes 4 bytes, and twice: in the draft and in the EditableImage. A 1024 × 1024 canvas is about 8 MB. On phones keep no more than a couple of small canvases.

chunks.heading: How do I save the picture?
chunks.text: Take a copy of the buffer: local copy = buffer.create(buffer.len(canvas:GetBuffer())) buffer.copy(copy, 0, canvas:GetBuffer()) local snapshot = Bloom.Texture.New(canvas.res_x, canvas.res_y, copy, false) Later you can draw it back with canvas:DrawTexture(snapshot, 1, 1).

chunks.heading: How do I make a mouse painting app?
chunks.text: local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService") local BRUSH = Color4.New32Bit(255, 80, 160) local last: Vector2? = nil UserInputService.InputChanged:Connect(function(input) if input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement then return end if not UserInputService:IsMouseButtonPressed(Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1) then last = nil return end local position = Vector2.new(input.Position.X, input.Position.Y) - frame.AbsolutePosition + Vector2.one if last then canvas:DrawLineAA(last.X, last.Y, position.X, position.Y, 4, BRUSH) end last = position canvas:Update() end)

chunks.heading: Does Bloom use the graphics card?
chunks.text: No. Everything is computed on the processor in Luau. But Bloom has --!native and --!optimize 2 turned on, so the code runs fast.

chunks.heading: Where are the tests?
chunks.text: In the tests folder. Run them: rokit install lune run tests/run
